label: AB4C_hP18_181_c_k_d-001
title: $\beta$-Berlinite (AlPO$_{4}$) Structure
comments:
This is the high-temperature form of berlinite, the analog of \href{current_web_home_dir/A2B_hP9_180_i_d-001}{$\beta$-quartz ($C8$)}. 
 Below 853K (Ng, 1976) it transforms into $\alpha$-berlinite in the \href{current_web_home_dir/ABC4_hP18_152_a_b_2c-001}{alarsite (AlAsO$_{4}$) structure}. 
 Our \href{current_web_home_dir/Tutorials/SiO2_AlPO4}{silica and aluminum phosphate page} has much more about the relationship between these structures. 
 We originally found this structure described in (Muraoka, 1997), but their aluminum and phosphorous coordinates are inconsistent with the Al-O and P-O distances and bond angles, so we use this earlier work. 
 Like $\beta$-quartz, this structure is \href{current_web_home_dir/Tutorials/ChiralSpaceGroups/index.html#ClassII}{chiral, Sohncke Class II}, and so may also be found in the enantiomorphic space group $P6_{2}22$ \#180. 
 (Ng, 1976) put the phosphorous atoms on the (3c) Wyckoff postion, but the AFLOW Wyckoff ordering protocol shifts the origin of the $z$-axis by c/2, moving the aluminum atoms to the (3c) site.
